D.t: Hannah Pingree leads by 13.7 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 101,122 votes; a one point swing is about 3,704 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +6.0 and D +21.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +11.3. Your best recent poll is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +8.3. 10 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cumberland, a projected net 79,198 votes; York, a projected net 22,556 votes; Knox, a projected net 6,419 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +6.5, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, D +2.5, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +0.7, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +6.3, 4.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Hannah Pingree runs furthest behind in Aroostook, Piscataquis, Penobscot. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 52 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 54 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.83 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 49 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Hannah Pingree: Immigration voters 26 to 65, Men 47 to 45, Voters who can afford daily costs 47 to 44. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.2M cash against $395K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 50% of the 179,532 ballots in Maine so far, against 21% for the other party. That is 2.2 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
Money: Raised $509K against $1.2M for Hannah Pingree.

R.t: Bobby Charles trails by 13.7 and wins 1% of simulations. Closing it takes about 50,561 voters switching sides, or 101,122 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +21.0 and D +6.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +11.3. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at D +8.3; your worst is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3. 10 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Aroostook, a projected net 7,439 votes; Somerset, a projected net 5,693 votes; Penobscot, a projected net 4,983 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +6.5, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, D +2.5, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +0.7, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +6.3, 4.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Bobby Charles runs furthest behind in York, Knox, Cumberland. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 40 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 76% of voters, 38 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.83 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 42 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Bobby Charles: Health care and Social Security voters 22 to 70, Large counties 24 to 68, College graduates 34 to 58. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$395K cash against $1.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
